questions.question: When should drivers obey posted speed limits?

options.text: Only when police officers are present

questions.explanation: Always obey speed limits. Check your speedometer regularly to make sure you are driving at a legal speed.

questions.question: When should you fasten your safety belt?
questions.explanation: Fasten your safety belt before you start the engine. The law requires drivers to use seat belts when driving.

questions.question: A pedestrian with a guide dog is waiting to cross in front of you at a corner. You want to turn right. What should you do first?

options.text: Turn off your engine until the person crosses the street.
Tell the pedestrian when to cross the street.
Wait until the person crosses the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the person crosses the street.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes must always have the right-of-way. Let them cross completely before you turn.

questions.question: What should you do before changing lanes or passing another vehicle?

options.text: Check your blind spots and mirrors.
Signal your intention before changing lanes.

questions.explanation: Always signal before you change lanes. Check your mirrors and turn your head to check your blind spot before you move your vehicle left or right.

questions.question: When must you stop your vehicle?

options.text: When a police officer tells you to stop.

questions.explanation: Stop completely at red traffic lights. Always obey police officers directing traffic, even if signs or signals say otherwise.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a person crossing the street with a white cane or guide dog?

options.text: Stop until the person is well away from your path of travel.
Honk your horn as you proceed past them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the person is well away from your path of travel.
questions.explanation: Stop completely when you see someone using a white cane or guide dog to cross. Always give blind pedestrians the right-of-way.

questions.question: At intersections where all corners have stop signs, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: Drivers should always offer to let other cars proceed first.

questions.explanation: Vehicles proceed in the order they arrive at the intersection. Come to a complete stop and yield to any vehicle that got there before you.

questions.question: You see animals standing near the roadway. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to scare them away.
Slow down and proceed with caution.
Quickly swerve into the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: Slow down if you see animals near the road. They may suddenly move into your path. There may also be more animals you cannot see.

questions.question: What is this bicyclist signaling?
questions.explanation: Bicycles do not have turn signals. Bicyclists use arm signals instead. A left arm straight out means they are turning left.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You should stop for other traffic.
Traffic is entering from another road. Give drivers space to safely merge into traffic.
Traffic is entering from another road and you should keep right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is entering from another road. Give drivers space to safely merge into traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic will merge into your lane. If possible, move to another lane to give merging drivers a clear path.

questions.question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?

options.text: Whenever you need to use them.
Before you get into the car.

questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors before you move your vehicle. Before driving, also adjust your seat, fasten your safety belt, and secure any items. Do not adjust mirrors while driving.

questions.question: How do alcohol and drugs affect driving skills?
questions.explanation: Alcohol and drugs harm many driving skills. They slow your reaction time, reduce coordination and alertness, and weaken your ability to concentrate.

questions.question: When driving in fog, which headlights should you use?
questions.explanation: Use low beams when driving in fog, rain, or snow. High beams reflect off the weather and make it harder to see.

questions.question: When you see this sign, you should stop and:

options.text: Check for vehicles in the direction you plan to go, then proceed.
Let all vehicles that arrive before or after you go first.
Check for traffic in all directions before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for traffic in all directions before proceeding.
questions.explanation: At a stop sign, you must come to a full stop. Look both ways and in all directions before you drive.

questions.question: Only ____ can lower blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
questions.explanation: Only time allows your body to remove alcohol from your system. Eating and drinking cannot speed this up.

questions.question: Orange-colored signs are:
questions.explanation: Orange signs are used in work zones. They are diamond-shaped with black letters or symbols. They warn drivers that workers are on or near the road.

questions.question: If the road is wet or icy, you should:
questions.explanation: Wet or icy roads reduce tire grip. You should slow down to stay safe.

questions.question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your nervous system. It reduces alertness, increases reaction time, and hurts coordination.

questions.question: If pedestrians cross illegally in the middle of the street instead of at a crosswalk, you:

options.text: Do not have to stop for them.
Should honk your horn at them.

questions.explanation: You must yield to all pedestrians. Even if they are crossing illegally, you must stop for them.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign shows that you cannot turn in the direction of the arrow. In this case, no right turns are allowed.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: An octagonal sign always means stop. You must come to a complete stop. Stop at the stop line, or before the crosswalk or intersection if there is no line.

questions.question: When you see a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog:

options.text: Honk to alert them to your presence.

questions.explanation: Pedestrians with a white cane or guide dog must be given the right-of-way. Always let them cross safely.

questions.question: If you approach a railroad crossing with no safety barrier, you should:

options.text: Assume trains don't usually cross there.
Cross the tracks only after looking both ways for an oncoming train.
Quickly cross the tracks if you think you can beat an oncoming train.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross the tracks only after looking both ways for an oncoming train.
questions.explanation: Look both ways for trains before crossing. Never try to beat a train across the tracks.

questions.question: Tailgating (driving too close to another car's bumper):

options.text: Can frustrate other drivers and make them angry.
Cannot result in a traffic citation.
Reduces collisions by preventing being "cut off."

questions.correctAnswerText: Can frustrate other drivers and make them angry.
questions.explanation: Tailgating is unsafe and can lead to aggressive driving. You may face legal consequences for driving unsafely.

questions.question: If you have an argument with someone and feel angry, you should:

options.text: Loudly play the radio while driving so you won't think about it.
Take a few minutes to calm down before driving.
Drive on the interstate to let off steam.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down before driving.
questions.explanation: Your emotions affect your driving. If you are angry, calm down before you drive. You need to focus on driving safely.
